Ishan Verma:

I welcome you all to the Q2 FY27 Earnings Conference Call of Adani Power 
Limited. We have with us today from the management, Mr. S.B. Khyalia, CEO; Mr.

Shersingh B. Khyalia: 
Good morning, friends. Welcome to our Quarter 2 earnings call. Thank you for 
joining us today. Our quarterly results and analyst presentation are available on 
the stock exchanges and our website. I hope you have gone through them 
already. Joining me today on this call are our CFO, Mr. Dilip Jha; and our Investor 
Relations Head, Mr. Nishit Dave. 
 
The recently concluded quarter has been another blockbuster quarter for us. 
Power demand has been strong and power selling rates are high. We have seen 
healthy volume growth on the same operating capacity year-on-year. As a result, 
we have seen strong growth in revenues and EBITDA and ended the quarter with 
a solid profit after tax of INR7,000 crores. We have also moved closer to 
commissioning the first unit of our ongoing capacity expansion projects. 
 
Now coming to the power market first. India needs abundant and reliable 
baseload power supply using domestic coal. This is especially important in times 
of 
geopolitical 
uncertainty, 
changing 
weather 
patterns 
and 
rapid 
industrialization. 
 
Domestic coal-based power remains vital to India's energy security and economic 
growth. India's power demand rose 11.5% year-on-year to 502 billion units in 
Quarter 2 with lower hydropower output because of weak monsoons. Coal and

lignite stepped up supply 73% of incremental generation needed to meet the 
demand. The average thermal PLF increased to 68% from 62% a year earlier. 
 
Now coming to Adani Power's performance in this backdrop. We achieved power 
sales growth of 11.5% and supplied 26.4 billion units in this quarter, and our PLF 
improved to 70%. This was supported by a high level of plant availability across 
our portfolio. This strong operating performance delivered record quarterly 
results. Total continuing revenue rose almost 30% to more than INR17,000 
crores. Continuing EBITDA rose by more than 18% to INR6,300 crores. This 
reflects the strength of our core portfolio despite higher fuel prices. 
 
Reported EBITDA rose by 46% to more than INR8,700 crores. Consolidated profit 
after tax rose 142% to more than INR7,000 crores. This was supported by strong 
operating profit and onetime prior period revenue. 
 
For H1, total continuing revenue was nearly INR35,500 crores, continuing EBITDA 
was INR13,300 crores and profit after tax was nearly INR12,000 crores.  
 
Quarter 2 was also an important quarter for our corporate structure, financial 
profile and capacity expansion. 
 
Adani Power's credit rating was upgraded from AA to AA+. The upgrade reflects 
our operating track record, strong cash flows, market leadership, revenue 
visibility and balance sheet flexibility. We received a letter of award for a 25-year 
PPA of 1,320 megawatts from Uttarakhand Power Corporation Limited during this 
quarter. It will be supplied from the upcoming Korba 2 power project. 
 
We have now secured long-term PPAs for 62% of our upcoming 24 gigawatt 
thermal pipeline. We were declared the successful resolution applicant for GVK 
Energy Limited under the CIRP process. This marks our entry into hydro 
generation through the operational 330-megawatt Alaknanda plant in 
Uttarakhand. 
 
We are expanding into dispatchable green energy by expanding our project 
portfolio in Bhutan. We signed a shareholders' agreement with Druk Green Power, 
our project partner, for a 770-megawatt hydropower project. The project will be 
developed through a 49:51 joint venture. It is our second joint development in 
Bhutan after the 570-megawatt Wangchhu hydro project.  
 
We are progressing quickly and steadily on our 24-gigawatt thermal capacity 
pipeline. At Korba Phase-II, the first 660 MW unit has been achieved grid 
synchronization. Commercial commissioning is expected shortly. The second unit 
is planned for quarter 4 of '27. 
 
The 1,600 MW Mahan Phase-II project is also at an advanced stage. Commercial 
operations are targeted for early Financial Year '28. Similarly, Raipur Phase-II,

second long-term PPA to Maharashtra DISCOM. 
 
In conclusion, India needs more than 100 gigawatts of new thermal capacity by 
2032. Adani Power has the execution capability, fuel logistics and balance sheet 
to support this growth. We remain committed to reliable, cost competitive round-

Thank you, sir, and good morning, everyone. I will walk you through our financial 
and operating performance for Quarter 2 FY27. I will provide you an update on 
our balance sheet, debt metrics and liquidity position. As Khyalia Sahab 
highlighted, Quarter 2 FY27 was marked by intense demand growth, which was 
driven by economic momentum and a weak monsoon. Peak demand reached 270 
gigawatts and power exchanges saw substantial tariff increase. In this 
environment,  
 
Adani Power delivered an outstanding operational quarter: Plant load factor 
increased to 70.1% in quarter 2 FY27 from 62.8% in quarter 2 FY26. For H1 FY27, 
PLF reached 74.1% against 64.8% last year. Consolidated sales volume expanded 
by 11.5% to 26.4 billion units in Quarter 2 FY27, compared to 23.7 billion units in 
Quarter 2 of last year. H1 '27 volume grew 14.3% to 55.1 billion units. 
 
Sales under long-term and medium-term PPAs expanded by 29.7% to 23.4 billion 
units, reflecting increasing offtake by DISCOMs. We also have a larger capacity 
operating under PPAs now as compared to last year. PPA realization improved by 
12.7% on a continuing basis, supported by the pass-through of import coal indices 
and recent medium-term PPAs. 
 
Merchant and short-term volume were 43% lower year-on-year as we strategically 
tied up previously-open capacities under medium-term contract. However, short-
term merchant tariffs surged by 33% per unit, capturing strong demand 
momentum. 
 
Turning to revenue, Our Continuing Revenue from Operations for Q2 FY27 grew 
by 29.8% to Rs. 17,014 Crore, up from Rs. 13,106 Crore in Q2 FY26. This was driven 
by higher dispatch volumes and stronger realization across both PPA and 
merchant segments. Our continuing other income was Rs. 514 Crore versus Rs. 
533 Crore in Q2 FY26. Our total continuing revenue stood at INR17,528 crores, 
which is 28.5% higher year-on-year basis. For H1 FY27, total continuing revenue 
stood at INR35,464 crores, which is 27.5% higher. During the quarter, we

Including these onetime items, total reported revenue for Q2 FY27 reached 
INR19,951 crores. H1 FY27 total reported revenue stood at INR39,273 crores. 
 
Now addressing our cost structure and bottom-line delivery. Total fuel cost for 
Q2 FY27 increased by 41.8% to INR10,229 crores, compared to INR7,216 crores in 
Q2 of last year. This rise was driven by increased volumes, coupled with an 
approximate 50% increase in the landed cost of imported coal. For H1 FY27, fuel 
cost stood at INR19,769 crores, higher by 36% Y-o-Y.. 
 
Our continuing EBITDA for the quarter for FY27 was INR6,321 crores, compared 
to INR5,333 crores in quarter 2 of last year. H1 FY27 continuing EBITDA grew by 
20.1% to INR13,304 crores. Reflecting the recognition of prior paid items, 
reported EBITDA grew by 45.7% to INR8,743 crores in quarter 2 FY27. Finance 
costs for the quarter decreased by 9.7% to INR760 crores in compared to INR842 
crores in Q2 of last year, driven by disciplined debt and liquidity management. For 
H1 '27, finance costs were INR1,662 crores. 
 
Continuing Profit Before Tax rose by 32.5% to INR4,370 crores in Q2 FY27 from 
INR3,298 crores in Q2 of last year. Reported Profit Before Tax grew by 71.2% to 
INR6,792 crores. The quarter included a net tax credit of INR231 crores, which is 
due to the reversal of provisions made earlier following the amalgamation of 
subsidiaries with Adani Power. 
 
As a result, Consolidated Profit After Tax for Q2 FY27 rose sharply by 141.5% to 
INR7,019 crores, compared to INR2,906 crores in Q2 of last year. For the first half 
of FY27, PAT stood at INR11,886 crores, representing a 91.4% increase year-on-
year basis. 
 
Moving to our balance sheet and capital position. We have kept a tight control 
on borrowings. We are funding our capex primarily through internal accruals. We 
rely on debt only to the extent of any gap between accruals and capex funding 
requirements. As of September 30, 2026, total debt stood at INR61,860 crores, 
compared to INR53,556 crores as of March '26. Net debt stood at INR45,846 
crores as of September 30, 2026, compared to INR45,022 crores as of March 31, 
'26. Some of the funds drawn down by us near the end of the quarter are 
reflecting as cash balance. 
 
Our liquidity profile remains strong, enabling us to support our brownfield and 
greenfield capex program, predominantly through internal cash accruals while 
maintaining conservative leverage metrics. The recent credit rating upgrade to 
AA+ by CARE Ratings and India Ratings acknowledges this financial discipline, 
robust liquidity buffers and predictability of cash flow.

In summary, quarter 2 FY27 has been an excellent quarter for Adani Power. Sales 
volume increased by 11.5% to INR26.4 billion unit with an operating PLF of 70.1%. 
Total continuing revenue grew by 28.5% to INR17,528 crores, with continuing 
EBITDA expanding to INR6,321 crores. Reported PAT grew by 141.5% to INR7,019 
crores. 
 
Our rating upgrade to AA+ and the operationalization of our subsidiary 
amalgamation significantly strengthened our capital profile and structural 
efficiency. Our organic expansion projects are progressing on schedule, backed 
by disciplined and self-funded capital allocation strategy. 
 
Thank you for your time and continued support. We are now ready to take your 
questions, if any. Thank you.
